item.title: Trump and Netanyahu clash in tense call over Iran peace framework
item.description: President Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu held what sources described as a "lengthy and dramatic" phone call Tuesday evening over a proposed framework to end the war with Iran, exposing a widening rift between the two allies over how to conclude the months-long conflict.

item.title: IRGC warns war will spread beyond Middle East if US resumes strikes
item.description:
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps issued a stark warning on Wednesday that any renewed American or Israeli military action against the country would trigger a conflict extending far beyond the Middle East, promising "crushing blows in places you cannot even imagine."

The threat came as diplomatic signals suggested a potential path toward ending the nearly three-month-old war between the US-Israel coalition and Iran. President Donald Trump told lawmakers that the conflict could end "very quickly," while Vice President JD Vance said negotiations with Tehran are "in a pretty good spot," adding that "a lot of good progress is being made."

item.title: Beijing delays Pentagon official's visit over Taiwan arms deal
item.description:
Beijing is stalling a planned visit by Elbridge Colby, the Pentagon's under-secretary of defense for policy, as China pressures President Donald Trump over a $14 billion weapons package for Taiwan, according to a Financial Times report published Wednesday.

The delay comes just days after Trump's two-day summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing on May 14-15, during which Taiwan emerged as one of the most contentious issues. Reuters was unable to independently confirm the details of the FT report.

item.title: Ukrainian drone strikes bring central Russia's oil refining to a standstill
item.description: A sustained campaign of Ukrainian drone strikes has forced virtually all major oil refineries in central Russia to halt or scale back fuel production, bringing refining operations across the region to a near-standstill, Reuters reported on May 20. The disruptions mark one of the most concentrated blows to Russian energy infrastructure since the start of the full-scale war.

item.title: Merz proposes EU 'associate membership' for Ukraine
item.description:
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has formally proposed granting Ukraine "associate member" status in the European Union, outlining the plan in a letter to EU chiefs Ursula von der Leyen and António Costa made public on Thursday.

The proposal would allow Ukraine's leader to attend EU summits and ministerial meetings without voting rights, while Kyiv would also gain a non-voting representative on the European Commission and non-voting members of the European Parliament.

item.title: Turkey sends flights to repatriate Gaza flotilla activists detained by Israel
item.description:
Israel has begun deporting approximately 430 activists detained from the Global Sumud Flotilla after Israeli naval forces intercepted the Gaza-bound aid convoy in international waters west of Cyprus, a move that has triggered a wave of international condemnation intensified by a video posted by far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir showing him taunting bound detainees.

The deportations, confirmed on Wednesday, follow days of mounting diplomatic fallout after Ben-Gvir shared footage of himself confronting kneeling activists with their hands zip-tied behind their backs, waving an Israeli flag and reportedly shouting "We are the masters" as Israel's national anthem played in the background. Turkey said on Thursday it was sending charter flights to Israel to repatriate its nationals among the detained activists.

item.title: Iran's Supreme Leader orders enriched uranium to stay in country
item.description: A directive from Iran's Supreme Leader that the country's near-weapons-grade enriched uranium must remain on Iranian soil jolted markets on Thursday, erasing much of the optimism that had briefly lifted investor sentiment a day earlier.

item.title: Iran restarted drone production during ceasefire, US intelligence finds
item.description:
Iran has restarted drone production during the six-week ceasefire that began in early April, rebuilding its military industrial base at a pace that has caught US intelligence agencies off guard, CNN reported Thursday citing four sources familiar with the assessments.

The reporting contradicts weeks of public assurances from Trump administration officials and military leaders who characterized Iran's military as crippled beyond near-term repair following Operation Epic Fury, the US-Israeli bombing campaign that began in late February.

item.title: Iran seeks permanent Hormuz toll system in talks with Oman
item.description:
Iran is in active discussions with Oman to establish a permanent toll system for maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, seeking to formalize what has been an ad hoc fee regime since the conflict with the United States and Israel erupted earlier this year.

Iranian Ambassador to France Mohammad Amin-Nejad told Bloomberg on Wednesday that "Iran and Oman must mobilize all their resources both to provide security services and to manage navigation in the most appropriate manner." The statement represents Tehran's clearest articulation yet of its intent to make the toll arrangement a lasting feature of Gulf commerce rather than a wartime stopgap.

item.title: Lithuania confirms crashed drone was Ukrainian
item.description:
A suspected drone entering Lithuanian airspace from Belarus on Wednesday triggered the first air alert in an EU and NATO capital to order civilian shelters since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, forcing President Gitanas Nausėda, Prime Minister Inga Ruginienė, and members of parliament into bunkers while Vilnius Airport suspended flights and train services were halted.

The alert, sent to mobile phones at around 10:20 a.m. local time, read: "Air raid alert! Go immediately to a shelter or a safe place, take care of your family members and wait for further instructions". Within minutes, residents across the capital descended into basements and underground parking garages. "I got dressed and went down to the basement," photographer Andrej Vasilenko told AFP. "My child was at school and had gone down into a shelter, so I felt reassured. It was strange, but at the same time so many people in Ukraine have been living with this for four years".

item.title: Iran says US proposal 'narrowed the gaps' as House eyes war powers vote
item.description:
Iran said Wednesday it is reviewing Washington's latest response to its peace proposal aimed at ending the nearly three-month conflict, as President Donald Trump warned that negotiations are on the "borderline" between a deal and renewed strikes.

The Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said Tehran had "received the US perspectives and is in the process of reviewing them," according to the Iranian state news agency Nour News. Iran also said the latest US proposal had "narrowed the gaps" between the two sides.

item.title: Iran says US proposal narrowed gaps but uranium, toll disputes persist
item.description: Iran indicated on Thursday that the latest American proposal has partially reduced differences between the two sides, even as it prepares a formal response to a plan that would see the Strait of Hormuz reopened and the US naval blockade of Iranian ports lifted. However, a dispute over Iran's push for a permanent toll system in the waterway and Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei's reported refusal to surrender Tehran's enriched uranium stockpile threaten to derail progress toward a lasting peace.

item.title: Trump to send 5,000 additional troops to Poland, reversing earlier cuts
item.description:
President Donald Trump announced Thursday that the United States will send an additional 5,000 troops to Poland, a reversal that comes just days after the Pentagon characterized its earlier cancellation of a similar-sized deployment as merely a "temporary delay."

"We will put more there if they want it," Trump said, emphasizing that Washington works "very closely" with Warsaw.

item.title: Rutte says many NATO allies 'not spending enough' on Ukraine
item.description: NATO foreign ministers convened in Helsingborg, Sweden, on Thursday for a two-day meeting focused on sustaining long-term support for Ukraine, with Secretary General Mark Rutte warning that many alliance members are "not spending enough" to help Kyiv defend itself against Russia's full-scale invasion.

item.title: Trump, Rubio reject Iran's plan for Hormuz toll system
item.description: Iran is in active talks with Oman to establish a permanent toll system for ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz, formalizing Tehran's control over one of the world's most critical maritime chokepoints. The move drew sharp rebukes from both President Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Thursday.

item.title: Russia developing seabed nuclear missiles, German investigation finds
item.description:
NATO intelligence services have been closely tracking Russia's Northern Fleet amid growing concerns that Moscow is advancing a secret program to deploy nuclear-armed missiles on the Arctic Ocean seabed, according to an investigation published on May 21 by German public broadcasters WDR and NDR. The report identifies a classified project codenamed "Skif," under which Russia is believed to be developing remote-controlled missile systems housed in sealed containers dropped from submarines to the ocean floor.

The revelation comes as Russia wraps up its largest nuclear exercises in years, a three-day drill running from May 19 through May 21 that mobilized nearly 65,000 troops, over 200 missile launchers, 140 aircraft, 73 surface vessels, and 13 submarines — including eight strategic nuclear submarines.

item.title: Palestinian envoy drops UN vice presidency bid after US threats
item.description: Palestinian Ambassador Riyad Mansour has withdrawn his candidacy for a vice president position at the UN General Assembly following pressure from the Trump administration, the United Nations confirmed on Thursday. Lebanon's ambassador will assume the role in his place.

item.title: NATO allies bewildered by Trump's troop reversal
item.description: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio arrived in Helsingborg, Sweden, on Friday for a NATO foreign ministers' meeting, carrying a message from President Donald Trump about allied shortcomings during the Iran conflict while trying to calm growing European anxiety over Washington's shifting military commitments on the continent.

item.title: Rubio cites 'slight progress' in US-Iran peace talks
item.description:
Pakistani Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi met Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi in Tehran as Islamabad pushed to narrow the remaining gaps between Washington and Tehran in stalled peace negotiations. Speaking at a NATO foreign ministers' meeting in Helsingborg, Sweden, Secretary of State Marco Rubio offered a cautious assessment of the diplomatic efforts.

"There has been some slight progress. I don't want to exaggerate it, but there's been a little bit of movement, and that's good," Rubio told reporters on Friday.

item.title: WHO upgrades Congo Ebola risk to 'very high' as cases surge
item.description:
The World Health Organization on Friday upgraded its risk assessment for the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo from "high" to "very high" at the national level, as the rapidly escalating epidemic now encompasses nearly 750 suspected cases and 177 suspected deaths.

WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said the outbreak is "spreading rapidly" and warned that the actual scale is likely far larger than official figures suggest. There are now 82 confirmed cases in the DRC along with seven confirmed fatalities, but Tedros indicated the true toll could exceed 1,000 infections, with cases significantly underreported for months before detection.
